newsitem.title: USA: DC won't need short-term debt under Clinton plan.
newsitem.headline: DC won't need short-term debt under Clinton plan.

text.p: The District of Columbia would no longer be forced to issue short-term financing to cover budget deficits under the fiscal reform plan proposed by President Clinton, D.C. Mayor Marion Barry said Tuesday.
The proposal would allow the city to borrow from the U.S. Treasury to cover all or part of its $400-$500 million accumulated deficit.

"As soon as this bill is passed and October 1 comes, we could requisition the Treasury for this money," Barry said at a news conference here. "That's a significant issue here because we can retire our accumulated deficit. We then are able to go to the bond market, not have to borrow short-term." That
might free the city to issue longer-term debt for capital spending, Barry said. The city will spend about $36 million to pay interest on this year's short-term borrowing, he said.
